10.1002_adfm.79174: Lithium‐metal all‐solid‐state batteries offer a pathway toward high‐specific‐energy storage but remain limited by instability at the solid‐state electrolyte (SSE)/Li interface. Fluorinated chloride solid electrolytes exhibit improved kinetic stability toward Li metal at low current densities (≤0.2 mA cm −2 ), but become increasingly susceptible to electron injection at high current densities (≥1 mA cm −2 ), leading to sustained reductive decomposition and interfacial degradation. Here, we develop LiCl‑deficient Li 3‑x InCl 5.2‑x F 0.8 solid electrolytes to regulate interfacial electron transport. LiCl deficiency generates Li vacancies preferentially at 4 g sites and lowers the barrier for In migration into these vacancies, thereby forming In‐on‐Li antisites. These antisite‐centered defect environments serve as electron‐localization centers that trap injected electrons, suppress long‐range electronic transport, and inhibit the reduction of In 3+ to metallic In. This electron‐localization mechanism promotes a self‐passivating interphase and markedly improves high‐current‐density compatibility with Li metal. The optimized Li 2.76 InCl 4.96 F 0.8 composition exhibits an ionic conductivity of 1.24 mS cm −1 , stable Li plating/stripping at 1.0–1.5 mA cm −2 , and durable full‐cell cycling with LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 (NCM622) cathodes at 1 mA cm −2 . These findings establish LiCl‐deficiency‐induced electron localization as an atomic‐scale electronic regulation strategy for enabling high‐current‐density compatibility between chloride solid electrolytes and Li‐metal anodes, thereby advancing the development of high‐specific‐energy all‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries.
10.1002_adma.202510685: Establishing a low‐resistance perovskite/ITO contact using self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) is crucial for efficient hole transport in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) without a pre‐deposited hole‐transporting layer. However, SAMs at the buried interface often encounter issues like nonuniform distribution and molecular aggregation during the extrusion process, leading to significant energy loss. Herein, a molecular hybrid bridging strategy by incorporating a novel small molecule is proposed, (2‐aminothiazole‐4‐yl)acetic acid (ATAA), featuring a thiazole ring and carboxylic acid group, along with the commonly used SAM, 4‐(2,7‐dibromo‐9,9‐dimethylacridin‐10(9H)‐yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (DMAcPA), into the perovskite precursor to synergistically optimize the buried interface. Composition analysis demonstrates that both molecules are effectively extruded to the bottom of the perovskite layer and form a well‐oriented hole‐selective contact interface through strong coordination between the anchoring groups and ITO substrate. The intermolecular interaction, along with the small molecular size of ATAA, enables its uniform dispersion among large DMAcPA, facilitating a compact molecular arrangement, effectively suppressing aggregation, and enhancing hole‐transporting efficiency. As a result, the inverted PSC employing this molecular hybrid strategy exhibits a power conversion efficiency as high as 26.64% (certified at 26.34%) and maintains 98.5% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h of continuous operation under 1‐sun illumination at the maximum power point.
10.1016_j.ensm.2026.104890: The transition toward sustainable and high-performance batteries requires not only advances in materials and architectures, but also the adoption of systematic approaches to experimental design. This review highlights the role of design of experiments (DoE) as a versatile and powerful methodology to accelerate innovation in the battery field. By replacing trial-and-error strategies with statistically sound frameworks, DoE enables the exploration of multiple variables and their interactions, offering deeper insights into complex phenomena that govern synthesis, performance, safety, recycling, and lifetime of batteries. Applications reviewed span from the optimization of electrode formulations and cathode synthesis to advanced thermal management strategies and recycling processes of end-of-life batteries. Across these domains, DoE has proven to reduce experimental redundancy, enhance reproducibility, and guide the identification of optimal operating conditions. The review also illustrates how DoE can act as a bridge between laboratory-scale research and industrial scalability, providing tools that are essential for the development of next-generation energy storage technologies. By presenting a comprehensive overview of its impact, this article aims to inspire researchers to embrace DoE as a cornerstone for systematic innovation, fostering both scientific progress and sustainable deployment of electrochemical energy storage.
10.1016_j.jclepro.2026.148463: The selective conversion of maleic acid (MA) to succinic acid (SA) is traditionally achieved by high-pressure catalytic hydrogenation. This route requires external hydrogen and significant energy input. Electrochemical reduction offers a viable alternative. It enables MA-to-SA conversion under ambient conditions and allows mechanistic control through electrode selection and current density. Cyclic voltammetry shows direct electron-transfer reduction of MA and SA on Cu electrodes. Ni displays negligible activity toward MA. Polarization studies indicate that Cu favors MA reduction, whereas Ni accelerates SA reduction. These trends highlight the influence of molecular structure on electrode–substrate interactions. Bulk electrolysis yields selective MA-to-SA conversion with Faradaic efficiencies up to 96 %. High electron-transfer rates are essential to suppress competing pathways. Stability tests reveal that SA undergoes over-reduction at high current densities, particularly on Ni. This finding emphasizes the need to balance productivity with product preservation. Complementary hydrogenation experiments broaden the valorization scope. Residence time and hydrogen availability govern selectivity, ranging from partially hydrogenated intermediates to deeply hydrogenated volatiles. Overall, the results support a dual-path electro-refinery strategy for sustainable SA production. The approach integrates mild electroreduction with controlled deep hydrogenation. It offers a scalable and low-carbon route for incorporating dicarboxylic acids into next-generation chemical and fuel manufacturing. • Copper enables efficient electrochemical reduction of maleic to succinic acid. • Nickel shows negligible activity for MA but favors SA kinetics under polarization. • Bulk electrolysis achieves high Faradaic efficiency under mild operating conditions. • Current density strongly governs selectivity and prevents undesired over-reduction. • Hydrogenation expands valorization, tuning products via residence time and H 2 supply.

10.1109_tmtt.2026.3747709: This article presents a digitally reconfigurable multimode backscatter rectenna integrated into a secure, battery-free wireless sensor node. The rectenna shares a common antenna among RF energy harvesting, backscatter-based long-range (LoRa) modulation and conventional long-range wide area network (LoRaWAN) transmission. The optimized design achieves a peak power-conversion efficiency of 30% at −4 dBm input RF power level and a 27.5 dB reflection contrast between its impedance states. An SF7/BW125 LoRa identification frame is generated through pulse wave modulation (PWM)-controlled impedance switching of the wireless power transfer (WPT) carrier and received on a frequency-shifted sideband by a standard LoRaWAN gateway. The backscatter identification frame precedes the conventional sensor-data uplink, providing an additional low-energy security channel without requiring a dedicated backscatter reader. Indoor experiments validated both communication links over the complete tested distance of 30 m, demonstrating the feasibility and long-range potential of LoRa-compatible backscatter communication for battery-free sensors.
